correctness.rationale: Independent exhaustive replay used the Singer model of PG(2,3): in F_27 with t³=t+1, the class of t generates F_27*/F_3*, of order 13, and the projective line spanned by 1,t has exponents {0,1,3,9}. Its thirteen distinct translates exhaust the lines. The replay tested every point subset, included exactly the proper labeled colorings, and generated all single-point toggles staying in that set. All exact distance layers from each source were computed. The graph was connected, with 468 vertices, 702 edges, degree 3 and every eccentricity 13; the only differences d−h were 0 and 2 with exact ordered counts 166608 and 52416. Every row contained 356 and 112, respectively. Reversing the order halves the positive-defect count, and the zero-defect tally contains the diagonal.
residual_risks: The certificate is finite and does not identify the abstract graph with F468 or support any extension to other planes.

evidence: Every six-point color class is the off-vertex part of a nonconcurrent line triple; each seven-point class is the complement of one such class. The indexed exact-metric theorem has the same valid masks and defect definition.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: PGL(3,3) acts transitively on nonconcurrent line triples (take three independent covectors to the coordinate covectors). It acts transitively on the six-point classes, and global complement exchanges their size with seven. These symmetries preserve both distances, so the number of defect-two targets is constant by source; the indexed count thus gives 52416/468=112. This uniformity does not follow from the aggregate number alone, but follows from that number and the known geometry.
